texts.preamble: Vijay Singh Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2022 Author: Deepak Kumar Agarwal
texts.facts: This revision has been filed by the petitioner being aggrieved by the judgment passed by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Sabalgarh, Distt. Morena, in Criminal Appeal No.40/2017, whereby the appeal filed by the applicant against the judgment dated 2.2.2017 passed by the JMFC, Sabalgarh, in Criminal Case No.1001/2006 has been rejected. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of this revision petition are that Complainant-Food Inspector, Food & Drugs Administration, Distt. Morena, filed a complaint against the applicant on the allegation that he took a sample of milk from Tanker No.MP06 E 1482 on 8.10.2002. The applicant was accompanying the said vehicle in which mixed milk was being transported. Aforesaid sample of the milk was sent to public analyst for his opinion. Report of the public analyst came to the effect that aforesaid sample of the mixed milk does not conform to the standards inasmuch as though the amount of fat was found to be sufficient at 5.5% , but the amount of "solids not fat" was found to be at lower end at 7.365% in place of 8.5%. Report of the public analyst was supplied to the applicant/accused. Thereafter charge was framed and evidence was recorded by the trial Magistrate. After conclusion of trial, applicant was convicted for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as "the Act") vide judgment dated 2.2.2017. Aggrieved by the conviction and sentence, applicant preferred an appeal before the Court of Session, which after hearing of above appeal, dismissed the same. This revision petition has been filed on the ground that applicant was held guilty for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act. As per the report of the public analyst, in the sample "milk solids not fat" was found below the prescribed standards. In these situation, case of the applicant will fall under Section 2(ia)(m) wherein lesser punishment is prescribed. It is further Vijay Singh Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94110936/ 1 submitted that compliance of mandatory provisions of Section 13(2) of the Act is not done. Learned counsel for the State supported the impugned judgment. Test for formalin was found positive, test for starch was found negative and test for added urea /fertilizer/detergent was found negative and BR reading at 40 degree Celsius (of extracted fact) was found to be 409.
texts.arguments: As per argument of learned counsel for the petitioner, as only solids not fat was found to be on lower side at 7.365% in place of 8.5%, case of the applicant will fall under Section 2(ia)(m) wherein lesser punishment is prescribed. The Apex Court in the case of Duli Chand Vs. Delhi Administration as reported in (1975) 4 SCC 649 has held that the jurisdiction of the High Court in a criminal revision application is severely restricted and it cannot embark upon a re-appreciation of evidence. The said judgment has been followed by the Apex Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Jagmohan Singh Kuldip Singh Anand and Others as reported in (2004) 7 SCC 659.
